summary:
Everything lives in one SQLite file, accessed through Prisma 7 with the PrismaBetterSqlite3 adapter. The client is created lazily behind a Proxy (src/lib/db/client.ts:43). There are 28 models, and every career table carries userId with ON DELETE CASCADE from users. The sources of truth are RaceViewingSession (an append-only log with watchedAt as a single instant), WatchedInterval (merged coverage, rewritten as a set) and XPTransaction (the ledger, deduplicated per account on the unique (userId, dedupeKey)). The counters on Race, RaceMastery, MilestoneProgress and the others are caches or landmarks. The adapter stores DateTime as ISO-8601 TEXT ('2026-09-22T18:18:21.101+00:00'), so every range query is a lexicographic text comparison. There is no raw SQL anywhere, and calendar bucketing is done in JavaScript using the machine's local time. User.timezone is never read.

Migrations are applied in two ways:
- **Installed app (packaged/standalone):** desktop/src/main.ts first takes a pre-update VACUUM INTO snapshot, but only when the version marker changes. desktop/src/migrate.ts then applies every unapplied prisma/migrations/*/migration.sql. Each migration runs in its own better-sqlite3 transaction with foreign keys OFF. The runner writes Prisma-compatible _prisma_migrations rows with sha256 checksums, and only after that does it start the Next child process.
- **Checkouts:** web dev and the tests use the Prisma CLI (npm run db:deploy / db:migrate). desktop:dev uses the same runner against the repository's endurance.db, with no snapshot.

One-time upgrade logic runs in src/instrumentation.ts register(). Next finishes register() before it answers any request, including the desktop /api/health probe. The 0.3.1 season reset keeps a per-account ConfigOverride marker ('seasonReset'), runs one Prisma transaction per account, logs failures and retries them on the next start, and createAccount pre-marks new accounts. That pattern carries over directly to a 0.4.0 backfill. Two limits apply: the desktop gives the server 60 s to become ready, and each Prisma transaction has a 60 s timeout.

db:recompute is a developer-only tsx script and is not shipped in the installer. It rebuilds race aggregates, then repairs the ledger and rebuilds totals, then re-syncs mastery, collections, achievements and milestones. It does not rebuild intervals from sessions, momentum, awards, challenges or the per-session snapshot columns.

There is no import, export or restore feature. Backup is Career → Back up career… (VACUUM INTO), and restore means replacing the file by hand. "Imported historical sessions" do not exist as a feature. Only the optional watchedAt field on the session schema exists: the UI form never sends it, and only scripts/seed.ts backdates sessions.
key_facts: MODELS (prisma/schema.prisma). User 153-202: account; unique name; timezone column never read anywhere in src/lib. UserSession 210-221: cookie token is the row id; idx (userId), (expiresAt). CareerProfile 224-258: careerXp BigInt, level, prestige, streaks, momentum; unique userId. Championship 264-287: unique (userId, slug). ChampionshipSeason 290-312: unique (championshipId, year); no userId, owned through championship.

Race 314-387: library entry plus cached aggregates (coverageSec, realViewingSec, timelineWatchedSec, sessionCount, furthestTimestampSec, avgPlaybackSpeed, startedAt, completedAt, lastWatchedAt, storyCompletedAt). iconicKey (349) groups recurring editions; raceMasteryId FK SetNull. Indexes: (userId, status), (userId, championshipId), (userId, seasonId), (userId, iconicKey), (userId, raceDate). No index on storyCompletedAt, completedAt or startedAt.

RaceViewingSession 390-428: append-only stint: start/endTimestampSec, playbackSpeed, timelineSeconds, realSeconds, newCoverageSeconds, coverageBefore/AfterSec, careerXpAwarded/seasonXpAwarded, watchedAt, createdAt, note. Indexes: (userId, watchedAt), (raceId, watchedAt). WatchedInterval 431-448: merged coverage, sessionId SetNull, idx (raceId, startSec), no userId.

RaceMastery 451-475: per-event lifetime row keyed by iconicKey; unique (userId, key); fields editionsTracked, editionsStoryComplete, totalRealSec, totalTimelineSec, first/latestCompletedYear, longestConsecutiveEditions. XPTransaction 482-518: source, amount, seasonAmount, sourceRef, sessionId SetNull, seasonPassId SetNull, careerXpAfter, levelAfter, dedupeKey. Unique (userId, dedupeKey) (migration 20260922203126); idx (userId, createdAt), (userId, source). No index on sessionId or sourceRef.

Achievement 521-540: GLOBAL definitions with no userId, unique key. AchievementProgress 542-560: unique (userId, achievementKey), idx (userId, unlockedAt). MilestoneProgress 563-579: unique (userId, metric, threshold), idx (userId, metric), reachedAt, valueAtReach, xpAwarded. Challenge/ChallengeProgress 585-630. SeasonPass/SeasonPassProgress 636-683. MasteryTree/Node/Progress 689-753 (kind RACE_EVENT uses iconicKey). Collection/CollectionItem 759-802 (item raceId Cascade). Trophy 804-827: metadata Json, idx (userId, awardedAt). HallOfFameEntry 829-856: snapshot Json, raceId SetNull, idx (userId, occurredAt). BudgetYear/BudgetWeek 862-909. MomentumHistory 911-927: unique and duplicate idx (userId, date). ConfigOverride 935-947.

MIGRATIONS: 20260922181417_init (all tables); 20260922191246_accounts (user_sessions plus a RedefineTables of users that adds avatarKey, accentKey, passwordHash, passwordSalt, lastActiveAt and unique name); 20260922203126_xp_dedupe_per_account (drops the global dedupeKey unique, adds (userId, dedupeKey)). Enum columns are plain TEXT with no CHECK constraint.

DATE STORAGE: @prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3 dist/index.js:412-417 binds a Date as toISOString().replace('Z', '+00:00') TEXT. Seen in a copy of endurance.db: watchedAt '2025-07-21T18:18:21.014+00:00' (text). SQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP would instead write 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', a different text shape that compares wrongly against the ISO values.

DESKTOP BOOT (desktop/src/main.ts:103-176): resolvePaths, then splash. If mode !== 'dev', takePreUpdateSnapshot runs (130-146). Then runMigrations (148), then startServer with READY_TIMEOUT_MS=60_000 (40, 159), then the window opens. recordVersion writes last-version.json only after the window has opened (224-228).

paths.ts:345-365: the database is <repo>/endurance.db in dev mode and <userData>/data/endurance.db otherwise. Migrations come from resources/migrations when packaged (electron-builder.yml:78-79 copies prisma/migrations there) and from prisma/migrations otherwise. Backups go to <userData>/backups.

RUNNER desktop/src/migrate.ts: journal_mode=WAL (90). foreign_keys=OFF outside any transaction (107), because a PRAGMA inside the per-migration transaction is a no-op. Each migration runs as database.exec(sql) inside database.transaction plus an insert into _prisma_migrations (147-161). A migration recorded as started but not finished throws (136-144). A checksum mismatch only warns and never re-applies (132). foreign_keys=ON at the end (172), with no PRAGMA foreign_key_check. Migration directories are sorted lexicographically (192-198); checksum is sha256 of the file bytes (207-211).

SNAPSHOT desktop/src/update-snapshot.ts: decideSnapshot (154-171) takes a copy when the database is non-empty and the marker version differs from the current one. The copy is VACUUM INTO backups/pre-update-<version>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.db (217-222); the newest 5 are kept (126). MANUAL BACKUP desktop/src/backup.ts:56-61: VACUUM INTO from a read-only connection, triggered by the menu item 'Back up career…' (menu.ts:259). Restore is manual per docs/install.md:90-92: close the app, replace endurance.db, delete the -wal and -shm files.

HEALTH GATE: desktop/src/server.ts:219-249 polls /api/health with a 3 s per-probe timeout until the 60 s deadline. Next queues every request until initialisation, including instrumentation register(), has finished: next/dist/server/lib/start-server.js:181-223 handlersPromise; node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/instrumentation.md:18 says register 'must complete before the server is ready to handle requests'.

0.3.1 HOOK: src/instrumentation.ts:17-30 runs when NEXT_RUNTIME==='nodejs', dynamically imports resetSeasonRewards, and wraps it in try/catch that logs. season-reset.ts: SEASON_RESET_KEY='seasonReset' (94) with value '0.3.1' (97); TRANSACTION_OPTIONS {maxWait: 15_000, timeout: 60_000} (108). The marker is written inside the same transaction (319). isSeasonResetApplied checks only that the row exists and ignores its value (152-158). resetSeasonRewards selects users with configOverrides.none({key}) (404-407) and handles one account per transaction. createAccount pre-marks both lastSeenVersion and seasonReset (src/lib/auth/accounts.ts:192-195). Covered by tests/integration/instrumentation.test.ts.

RECOMPUTE scripts/recompute.ts:50-101, for all accounts or one given by name or id: (1) recomputeAllRaces, one transaction per race (race-engine.ts:159-165); (2) repairXpLedger (session-engine.ts:583-625), which runs purgeOrphanedSessionXp, deletes stale story-complete:<raceId> bonuses, then rebuildCareerTotals and rebuildSeasonXpFromLedger; (3) one transaction (timeout 120 s) running ensureMasteryTrees, ensureSeasonCollections, recomputeRaceMasteries, syncCollections, syncMastery, computeCareerMetrics, syncAchievements, syncMilestones. It does NOT rebuild WatchedInterval from sessions, momentum/streaks, challenges, awards (trophies/Hall of Fame), budget weeks or the session snapshot columns. It runs through tsx and is not shipped: electron-builder files are only package.json and desktop/out.

rebuildCareerTotals (xp-ledger.ts:265-307) replays the whole ledger ordered by (createdAt, id) and issues one UPDATE for each row whose careerXpAfter/levelAfter changes. awardXp (xp-ledger.ts:58-134) has no way to set createdAt: every award is stamped at log time.

BACKDATING: session-engine.ts:93 sets watchedAt = input.watchedAt ?? now, but recomputeRaceAggregates is called with `now` (160), so storyCompletedAt = race.storyCompletedAt ?? now (race-engine.ts:87), i.e. the log time. logSessionAction reads the watchedAt form field (actions.ts:294), but log-session-form.tsx (fields 169-187) never sends it. Only scripts/seed.ts:289-302 backdates, passing now=watchedAt. In the dev DB copy, sessions start 2025-07-21 while every XPTransaction.createdAt is 2026-09-22.

SESSION SNAPSHOTS: RaceViewingSession.careerXpAwarded and seasonXpAwarded are never written (sum = 0 in the dev DB; logViewingSession's create at session-engine.ts:128-143 omits them). deleteViewingSession (465-560) rebuilds intervals and the race aggregates but never rewrites newCoverageSeconds or coverageBefore/AfterSec on the remaining sessions.

RACE DELETE: deleteRaceAction (actions.ts:266-282) only deletes the race. Sessions cascade away, and their VIEWING/REWATCH/STORY_COMPLETE XP rows keep their XP with sessionId set to NULL until repairXpLedger runs, which only the dev script does.

CONFIGOVERRIDE: key/value Json per account, unique (userId, key), accessed via the userId_key selector. Keys in use: 'seasonReset' (season-reset.ts:94), 'lastSeenVersion' (whats-new.ts:15), 'stintEntryMode' (preferences.ts:12), 'displayTitle' (domain/cosmetics.ts:21), 'defaultPlaybackSpeed' (actions.ts:516, settings/page.tsx:27). There are no global rows. The economy override loader that config/index.ts:22-24 and economy.ts:9-10 describe (src/lib/config/runtime.ts, loadConfig) does not exist.

PRISMA DIFF (verified with `prisma migrate diff`): adding a nullable column to races produces `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`. Adding `Boolean @default(false)` NOT NULL to races produces a full RedefineTables (new_races, copy, drop, rename). A new @@index produces CREATE INDEX. A new XPSource enum value produces an empty migration. A nullable DateTime column on race_masteries produces ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN.

ACCOUNT ISOLATION: requireUserId() (auth/session.ts:125-129) is the only source of identity, and the cookie holds only the UserSession id. Actions scope writes with updateMany/deleteMany using where {id, userId} (actions.ts:256, 273). recomputeRaceAggregates takes no userId, so ownership is a precondition (race-engine.ts:45-49). deleteAccount is user.deleteMany and relies on the cascades (accounts.ts:298-302). tests/domain/design-rules.test.ts:79-128 forbids hard-coded ids (the regex also matches the identifier USER_ID) and requires requireUserId() and force-dynamic on every page. tests/auth/account-isolation.test.ts covers races, stints, championships and dedupe.

EXISTING DEDUPE KEYS: story-complete:<raceId> (session-engine.ts:212), pass-tier:<passId>:<tier>, season-complete:<seasonId> (collection-engine.ts:584), achievement:<key> (achievement-engine.ts:485), milestone:<metric>:<threshold> (achievement-engine.ts:556), mastery:<treeKey>:<nodeKey> (mastery-engine.ts:984), challenge:<id>.

VERSION 0.4.0 must change in: package.json:3; package-lock.json:3 and :9; the first entry of src/lib/changelog.ts CHANGELOG (currently line 30); CHANGELOG.md, regenerated with `npm run changelog` (tests/domain/changelog.test.ts:27-52 enforce all of this). APP_VERSION reads package.json (src/lib/version.ts). The desktop reads app.getVersion() or package.json, which also names the pre-update snapshot and the installer artifacts (electron-builder.yml:105,109).
The XPSource union is duplicated in src/lib/domain/types.ts:21-24 and prisma/schema.prisma:84-99, so any new source has to be added in both places.

Test DB bootstrap: tests/setup.ts runs `npm run db:deploy` when prisma/migrations holds a migration that endurance-test.db lacks. tests/desktop/migrate.test.ts covers the fresh apply, the no-op re-run, the RedefineTables case keeping child rows, and checksum mismatch. Both pass: 26 tests across migrate plus update-snapshot.

overlaps.existing: Session history via race_viewing_sessions (userId, watchedAt); xpBySource(userId, from, to) at xp-ledger.ts:316-332 over (userId, createdAt); landmark timestamps AchievementProgress.unlockedAt, MilestoneProgress.reachedAt, Trophy.awardedAt, HallOfFameEntry.occurredAt; BudgetYear.annualBudgetHours (default 336) stored per year; stats-engine builds local-time day and month buckets in JavaScript from a three-column projection.
overlaps.recommendation: Derive chapters on read from sessions plus landmark tables; the indexes already cover year-range scans. Persist only a frozen snapshot per completed year, e.g. a new table unique on (userId, year) holding Json, following the existing Trophy.metadata and HallOfFame.snapshot pattern, so Wrapped stays stable after later edits. Attribute XP by year carefully: XPTransaction.createdAt is the log time, so XP for backdated sessions lands in the wrong year.

overlaps.existing: RaceMastery (race_masteries, unique (userId, key = Race.iconicKey)) with editionsTracked, editionsStoryComplete, totalRealSec, totalTimelineSec, first/latestCompletedYear and longestConsecutiveEditions. It is rebuilt from races on every stint by recomputeRaceMasteries (mastery-engine.ts:769-850), which also maintains Race.raceMasteryId. The RACE_EVENT MasteryTree keys on iconicKey. Rows are never emptied or deleted.
overlaps.recommendation: Extend RaceMastery rather than adding a parallel entity; that is the 'do not duplicate' constraint. Add nullable columns (verified to be ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN), for example customName, userCreatedAt, archivedAt, totalCoverageSec. recompute currently overwrites `name` with eventDisplayName(iconicKey) on every run (mastery-engine.ts:823, 836), so a user-set name needs its own column. iconicKey is free text (schemas.ts:110, optionalText(80)) and matched exactly, so a user-managed event needs a normalisation or merge operation. Otherwise renaming a key creates a new row, and legacy milestones could be earned again.

overlaps.existing: Race aggregates plus WatchedInterval, which gives the watched/unwatched timeline; RaceViewingSession (raceId, watchedAt), which gives sessions, the resume point (furthestTimestampSec) and elapsed time (startedAt to lastWatchedAt); TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR_CONFIG.longHaulThresholdSec = 12h (economy.ts:420); BudgetWeek and BudgetYear; the story-complete:<raceId> dedupe key and its revoke-on-coverage-loss rule (session-engine.ts:521-525).
overlaps.recommendation: Add a nullable per-race override column, e.g. Race.expeditionMode Boolean? (null means use the threshold). A NOT NULL default would force a full RedefineTables of races. Store the threshold as a per-account ConfigOverride key. Award checkpoint XP through awardXp with a dedupeKey such as expedition:<raceId>:<pct>. Decide whether a checkpoint is revoked when coverage drops, as the Story Complete bonus is. Store the permanent summary as frozen Json with raceId SetNull, following HallOfFame.

overlaps.existing: stats-engine already computes longest session, activity buckets and per-race figures (e.g. stats-engine.ts:2180-2253), with calendar bucketing in JavaScript by design (lines 44-53, 780-786). Indexes: (userId, watchedAt), (raceId, watchedAt), races (userId, raceDate).
overlaps.recommendation: Extend stats-engine. Add @@index([userId, storyCompletedAt]) on races if records such as Story Completes per year or month are queried in SQL; that is a plain CREATE INDEX. Compute 'unique coverage in a day' by replaying intervals, not from newCoverageSeconds, which is stale after deletions.

overlaps.existing: MilestoneProgress plus the MILESTONES ladders (config/milestones.ts: realHours HOUR_STEPS includes 100, 336, 500, 1000...10000; storyCompletes and racesCompleted COUNT_STEPS 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100...1000), paid through dedupe milestone:<metric>:<threshold>, with reachedAt set to the log time. HallOfFame FIRST and MILESTONE entries: first:race-completed, first:story-complete, first:race-12h, first:race-24h, milestone:stories:N, milestone:real-hours:N (awards-engine.ts:624-750).
overlaps.recommendation: Do not pay XP twice for the same threshold. Either make the new milestones a presentation layer with reconstructed timestamps (a new table unique on (userId, key) with achievedAt, valueAtReach and a sessionId SetNull pointer) that pays no XP where an existing rung already pays, or give them a distinct dedupe namespace and pay only for genuinely new rungs (6h first, 336 h in a calendar year, 5/10/25 editions of one event). The backfill should compute from session replay, not from Race.storyCompletedAt, which is the log time.

overlaps.existing: The 0.3.1 pattern: instrumentation register(), a per-account ConfigOverride marker, one transaction per account, retry on failure, and createAccount pre-marking.
overlaps.recommendation: Reuse it, with a versioned marker such as 'careerBackfill' = '0.4.0', compared by value rather than by presence, so a later algorithm change can re-run it. Keep each account's work well under both 60 s limits: the desktop readiness timeout and the Prisma transaction timeout. The marker lives inside the DB, so a restored older backup triggers the backfill again automatically.

risks: Blocking backfill: register() must finish before Next answers /api/health, and the desktop fails after 60 s with 'The server did not start within 60 seconds' (main.ts:40, server.ts:219-249). That kills the child, the transaction rolls back, and the next launch repeats the same thing, so the app never opens. The per-account Prisma transaction timeout is also 60 s (season-reset.ts:108). A 10-year backfill of tens of thousands of sessions has to be batched, split into phases each with its own marker, or moved off the startup path.

NOT NULL @default columns on existing tables generate a RedefineTables (verified: `Boolean @default(false)` on races). That is a full copy of the table; it is safe only because the runner disables FKs, and the runner never runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check afterwards. Prefer nullable columns (plain ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) on races, race_viewing_sessions and xp_transactions.

Timestamps written by SQL (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP defaults on rows inserted or backfilled in migration SQL) come out as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', while the adapter writes 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ' with Z replaced by '+00:00'. Range filters compare TEXT lexicographically, so same-day comparisons go wrong. Do data backfills in TypeScript through Prisma, not in migration.sql.

Migration hygiene for the custom runner: never edit an applied migration (a checksum change only warns and never re-applies). The name must sort after 20260922203126. The SQL must be valid inside a transaction (no VACUUM; PRAGMA statements are no-ops). A new UNIQUE index that existing data violates aborts startup with an error window; the DB stays intact but the app will not open.

Reverting to 0.3.2 after 0.4.0 has run: new enum values such as a new XPSource are stored as TEXT without a migration, and the older Prisma client would reject them on read. The pre-update snapshot is the only way back.

XP by year is misattributed for backdated sessions: awardXp always stamps createdAt at log time, and Race.storyCompletedAt uses `now` rather than watchedAt through the action path (session-engine.ts:160, race-engine.ts:87). 'Exact first-achieved timestamps' therefore have to come from replaying sessions ordered by watchedAt. watchedAt is one instant with no stint start, so interpolating inside a session assumes watchedAt means the end, which is how the UI logs it (after the fact).

Stale derived columns: newCoverageSeconds and coverageBefore/AfterSec are not rewritten after a session delete, and careerXpAwarded/seasonXpAwarded are always 0. Neither can be used for records or chronicle figures.

Existing exploits the new systems would inherit: deleting a race keeps its viewing and Story Complete XP, orphaned, because repair runs only through the dev script. Delete and recreate a race and story-complete:<newId> pays again. Any dedupe key based on raceId (expedition checkpoints) or on iconicKey/RaceMastery id (legacy milestones; renaming an iconicKey creates a new RaceMastery row) can be re-earned the same way.

Replaying the ledger costs one UPDATE per row: rebuildCareerTotals issues an UPDATE for every row after the change point. Inserting backfilled XP with historical createdAt values restamps most of the ledger, tens of thousands of Prisma round trips in a single transaction.

Missing indexes on FK columns used by SetNull/Cascade: xp_transactions.sessionId, watched_intervals.sessionId, collection_items.raceId, hall_of_fame_entries.raceId, races.raceMasteryId. Each deleted session scans these tables. Queries with dedupeKey startsWith compile to LIKE and do not use the (userId, dedupeKey) index.

logViewingSession already reads the entire session history and all races for every stint inside a 60 s transaction (metrics.ts:115-160). Adding chronicle, legacy and milestone evaluation there without incremental reads adds more per-stint cost that grows with the history.

Design rules to respect (tests/domain/design-rules.test.ts): only src/lib/server/upgrades/season-reset.ts may delete trophies, Hall of Fame entries, passes or challenges; no file may set unlockedAt, awardedAt or completedAt to null; engines may not write negative amounts or decrement counters; the identifier USER_ID is forbidden in server, auth and app files.
desktop:dev skips the pre-update snapshot and migrates the repository's endurance.db directly. db:recompute is not available to end users, so all repair and backfill logic has to live in the app.
questions_for_owner: 'Imported historical sessions' do not exist today. The only route is the optional watchedAt field, which the UI never sends; only the demo seed backdates. Should 0.4.0 add a real backdated-entry or bulk-import path? If so, should imported sessions pay XP, and should that XP be dated at watchedAt or at import time?

Should retroactive milestones and event-legacy awards found by the upgrade backfill pay XP? If they do, should the ledger rows be dated at the reconstructed historical time (correct XP-by-year and XP graph, but the ledger has to be restamped) or at upgrade time (the ledger stays append-only, but all back-paid XP appears in the 2026 chapter)?

Several of the new career milestones match rungs that already pay XP: 100/500/1000+ real hours, 10/25/50/100 Story Completes, 100+ races completed, first 12h and 24h. Should the new system pay only for rungs that are genuinely new, or pay nothing and act as a timeline with exact timestamps on top of the existing ladders? And may the backfill correct existing MilestoneProgress.reachedAt values, which are log times, to the reconstructed times?
Should the 0.4.0 backfill block startup, as the 0.3.1 reset does (the app opens only when it is done, with a 60 s ceiling), or run in the background with an 'Updating your chronicle…' state?
When coverage drops (a session is deleted), should expedition checkpoints and event-legacy milestones be revoked, as the Story Complete bonus is today, or kept as permanent landmarks?

Should deleting a race keep its chronicle, legacy and expedition-summary landmarks (the HallOfFame precedent is raceId SetNull)? And should 0.4.0 also close the existing gap where deleting a race keeps its viewing and Story Complete XP?

Is the machine's local time zone the right calendar for year boundaries (it is what the whole app uses today; User.timezone is stored but ignored)? And should a year's Wrapped be frozen permanently once the year ends, or always recomputed from current history?

area: Canonical viewing history and reward integrity (sessions, intervals, Story Complete, XP ledger, delete/edit paths)
summary:
Logging a stint has one write path: `logViewingSession` (src/lib/engines/session-engine.ts:88-405). It runs in a single interactive transaction and does four things. It appends a `RaceViewingSession` row. It rebuilds that race's merged `WatchedInterval` set from scratch. It rebuilds the race's cached aggregates (`recomputeRaceAggregates`). Then it pays XP through `awardXp`. The awards are viewing XP with no dedupe key, a Story Complete bonus keyed `story-complete:<raceId>`, and then the challenge, collection, mastery, achievement and milestone rewards, each with its own dedupe namespace. Trophies and Hall of Fame entries earn no XP.

Sessions are never edited in place. The only operations are create and delete. `deleteViewingSession` (session-engine.ts:465-545) first deletes the stint's VIEWING/REWATCH ledger rows. It then deletes the session, rebuilds coverage by replaying the remaining sessions in watchedAt order, and revokes the Story Complete row if the race is no longer complete. Finally it rebuilds career totals and season XP from the ledger. No row ever holds negative XP. Achievements, milestones, mastery, challenges, collections, pass tiers, trophies and Hall of Fame entries are never revoked.

A session stores only one wall-clock instant, `watchedAt`. The stint form never sends it (src/components/races/log-session-form.tsx:169-187), so it defaults to the moment of logging, which is effectively the END of the stint. With `realSeconds` (the wall-clock duration), the stint's wall-clock window can be taken as [watchedAt - realSeconds, watchedAt]. With `startTimestampSec`, `endTimestampSec` and `playbackSpeed`, it can be mapped linearly onto the race timeline. That is enough to work out when a milestone threshold was crossed partway through a session.

Every other event timestamp is the log time `now`, not `watchedAt`. That covers `storyCompletedAt`, milestone `reachedAt`, achievement and mastery `unlockedAt`, and `XPTransaction.createdAt`.

The main integrity gaps:
- `deleteRaceAction` revokes no XP, so delete-race-and-recreate re-earns viewing XP and the Story Complete bonus.
- Tiny races are allowed (the only lower bound on duration is > 0).
- Real-hour metrics ignore the XP speed guard: 0.1x in RANGE mode gives up to 480 real hours in one stint.
- A race can be marked Completed by hand, and that feeds milestones and season completion.
- Shrinking a race's runtime can make it Story Complete without watching the start, because intervals past the runtime still count.
- Changing a race's iconicKey, or tagging several races with the same key and year, farms event-mastery XP.
key_facts: RaceViewingSession (prisma/schema.prisma:390-428): startTimestampSec, endTimestampSec (race-timeline window, seconds), playbackSpeed Float, timelineSeconds (= end-start, includes rewatch), realSeconds (= round(timelineSeconds / clampSpeed(speed)), wall clock), newCoverageSeconds (never-before-seen timeline at LOG time, snapshot), coverageBeforeSec/coverageAfterSec (snapshots), careerXpAwarded/seasonXpAwarded (Int default 0 — NEVER WRITTEN by session-engine.ts:127-143, so race-detail-view.tsx:240 XP chip never renders), watchedAt DateTime @default(now()), createdAt, note. Indexes [userId, watchedAt], [raceId, watchedAt]. No wall-clock start column, no updatedAt.

watchedAt semantics: session-engine.ts:93 `const watchedAt = input.watchedAt ?? now`. The UI form (log-session-form.tsx:169-187) posts raceId, mode, entryMode, playbackSpeed, startTimestamp, endTimestamp, realMinutes, note — never watchedAt — so in practice watchedAt == log instant ≈ END of the stint. The server action still accepts `watchedAt` (actions.ts:294; schemas.ts:68-79 optionalDate) with NO past/future bound, so a crafted post can backdate or future-date it.

risks: Delete-race-and-recreate exploit: deleteRaceAction (actions.ts:266-279) leaves viewing XP (orphaned) and `story-complete:<oldRaceId>`. A recreated race has a new uuid, so re-logging pays viewing XP and the Story Complete bonus again, as often as you like. Any new race-keyed reward (expedition checkpoints, summaries) inherits this unless race deletion revokes race-bound XP the way stint deletion does.

Tiny-race farming: durationSeconds only requires > 0 (schemas.ts:19-49, max 48h). A 1-minute race with a 1-minute stint earns the 500 XP 'Sprint' Story Complete bonus (plus 150 season XP) and counts toward storyCompletes milestones, achievements and mastery. Any 'N Story Completes' or 'races completed' milestone needs a minimum-runtime or eligibility rule.

Speed and real-hours inflation: the XP guard (xpMinSpeed 0.75) protects XP only. realSeconds itself goes up to timeline/0.1: MIN_PLAYBACK_SPEED 0.1 is reachable via the defaultPlaybackSpeed setting (schemas.ts:221), which seeds the form's hidden speed input. RANGE mode has no real-time cap: a 48h race at 0.1x is 480h in one stint. The realHours milestones, the 336h-in-a-year milestone, and the longest-session and most-time-per-day PRs would all be inflatable. Credit time-based milestones and PRs with realSeconds capped at timelineSeconds / xpMinSpeed.

Log-then-delete harvesting: stint deletion revokes only VIEWING/REWATCH and a no-longer-valid STORY_COMPLETE. MILESTONE, ACHIEVEMENT, MASTERY_NODE, CHALLENGE, SEASON_COMPLETE and SEASON_PASS_TIER XP stay. So a fake stint can unlock landmarks, then be deleted while the landmark XP is kept. Each is one-time thanks to dedupe, but the career is permanently inflated. New v0.4.0 milestones inherit this unless their policy is decided explicitly.

Hand-marked Completed: setRaceStatusAction or createRaceAction with status=COMPLETED counts as completed in metrics (racesCompleted, circuits, countries, seasonsCompleted), collections (5,000 XP Season Complete via `season-complete:<seasonId>`, with a user-defined plannedRaceCount that can be 1) and mastery. It persists until that race is next recomputed. 'First race completed' and 'N races completed' milestones should use storyCompletedAt, or explicitly accept trust-based completion.

Runtime-shrink false Story Complete: intervals are not clamped to the runtime in fromRows or isStoryComplete (verified by probe). Watch hour 1-2 of a 2h race, edit actualDuration to 1h, and the race becomes Story Complete with 0-1h unwatched. updateRaceAction pays no bonus, but storyCompletes-driven milestones, achievements and mastery do count it.

Gap tolerance counted as coverage: addInterval bridges holes up to 20s and counts them in addedSeconds and coverage. Many short stints spaced 20s apart cover about 21x the time actually watched. Expedition percentages would inherit this.

Event-key farming (pre-existing): editionsStoryComplete in mastery-engine.ts:248-256 counts RACES per iconicKey, not distinct years. metrics.maxEditionsOfOneEvent counts years.length with duplicates (metrics.ts:232). ensureMasteryTrees never removes trees, so renaming an iconicKey creates a fresh `event:<newKey>` tree whose nodes (up to 25k XP) unlock again. Event Legacy must dedupe editions by (eventId, edition year/date) and key rewards by a stable event id.

Timestamp ambiguity for reconstruction: watchedAt is the log instant (≈ end) for UI-logged stints, but can be arbitrary (past or future, unvalidated) via the action. Batch-logging several stints at once gives identical watchedAt values that stack. A future watchedAt also freezes streaks (updateStreak ignores days <= lastActiveDate). Validate watchedAt <= now + slack, and define the reconstruction as start = watchedAt - realSeconds.

Stale snapshots: newCoverageSeconds, coverageBeforeSec and coverageAfterSec are never recomputed after an earlier stint is deleted. storyCompletedAt is cleared and re-stamped to a new log time when coverage dips and returns. completedAt is sticky and survives un-completion, and stats-engine.ts:1042/1297 counts 'completed in window' from it. Year-in-review and expedition summaries must replay sessions, not trust these fields.

Edit destroys history: there is no edit-in-place, and a re-logged stint gets today's watchedAt. Fixing a typo on a 31 Dec stint moves it to another year, changes reconstructed milestone times, and its Story Complete may be revoked and then re-paid.

Season XP drift: every stint delete runs rebuildSeasonXpFromLedger, which strips momentum boosts from all passes (ledger seasonAmount is unboosted). New checkpoint XP should use seasonAmount 0 or record the boost in the ledger.

Performance: rebuildCareerTotals (xp-ledger.ts:265-307) reads every XPTransaction and issues one UPDATE per row after the deleted one. Deleting an early stint in a 10-year, tens-of-thousands-of-rows career runs a very long UPDATE loop inside a 60s transaction (TRANSACTION_OPTIONS session-engine.ts:51). computeCareerMetrics loads all sessions and races on every stint (metrics.ts:120-165). Milestone backfill and chronicle aggregates should be incremental, or run at start-up with a marker, not on every stint.

Ordering: rebuildCareerTotals breaks createdAt ties by uuid `id`, which is random rather than insertion order. The delete path replays coverage by watchedAt, while logging order is createdAt. A 'which session crossed the threshold' replay must fix one canonical order (watchedAt, createdAt, id) and use it everywhere.
questions_for_owner: For stints logged through the UI, watchedAt is the moment of logging (≈ the END of the stint), and there is no start time. Should v0.4.0 define stint wall-clock start = watchedAt - realSeconds, and bucket years/days and reconstruct milestone crossings on that basis? Or should the form get an explicit 'when did you watch this' start time (a new nullable column, backfilled as watchedAt - realSeconds)?

Should a Year in Review attribute viewing to watchedAt but XP and levels to XPTransaction.createdAt (log time)? They differ for backdated or batch-logged stints. Or should chronicle XP be re-dated to the originating session's watchedAt where a sessionId exists?

When a stint is deleted, should the new Career Milestones and Event Legacy milestones be revoked (like the Story Complete bonus, re-earnable), or stay earned as landmarks (like achievements and existing milestones)? If they stay, should their exact first-achieved timestamp be recomputed from the remaining history or frozen?
Should hand-marked 'Completed' races (status COMPLETED without coverage) count toward 'first race completed', 'N races completed' and event editions, or only Story Complete?

Should one-time rewards be protected against delete-race-and-recreate? Options: make deleteRaceAction revoke race-bound XP (VIEWING/REWATCH/STORY_COMPLETE/new expedition keys) like stint deletion does, or key new rewards by recurring event plus edition year instead of race uuid.

Should milestones and PRs based on real time use the XP-guarded real time (timelineSeconds / max(speed, 0.75)) and cap per-day totals at 24h, so a 0.1x stint can't produce a 480-hour 'longest session' or cross the 336h/year milestone?

Should Event Legacy milestones that overlap the existing RACE_EVENT mastery nodes (1/3/5/10 editions, 3/5 consecutive, 50/150 hours) be XP-free badges, or should the mastery nodes be retired in favour of the legacy system? Paying both would double-pay the same accomplishment.
Should v0.4.0 add in-place stint editing that keeps the original watchedAt, so correcting a typo doesn't move a stint into the current year?
Is a minimum race runtime or minimum real watch time acceptable for Story Complete-based milestones and expedition eligibility, to close the tiny-race farming path?

area: Existing statistics, metrics and year handling (stats-engine, metrics, periods, budget, momentum, stats/career pages, charts)
summary:
Statistics are read-only and come from two engines. `src/lib/engines/stats-engine.ts` (2315 lines, no tests) powers `/stats` (`src/app/stats/page.tsx` → `getStatistics` + `getFilterOptions` → `StatisticsView` client component). It takes a `StatsFilter` (year, championshipId, seasonId, circuitSlug, raceType, min/maxRuntimeHours, status, storyCompleteOnly). The only time filter is a local calendar year (`yearWindow`). There is no arbitrary date range, and no filter for event (iconicKey) or single race. Totals and per-race sums come from Prisma `aggregate`/`groupBy` on `RaceViewingSession`. Day, month, year and week buckets are built in JS from a 3-column projection of every in-scope session (`loadActivityBuckets`), using server-process local time and the user's `User.weekStart`. XP over time is one ledger aggregate per month. `src/lib/engines/metrics.ts` `computeCareerMetrics` is the lifetime metric object. Achievements, milestones and awards use it, and it runs on every logged stint and on the dashboard and career pages. It reads all races and all sessions each time.

Definitions: "real viewing time" = `RaceViewingSession.realSeconds`, which is computed as timelineSeconds/playbackSpeed and is never measured. "Unique coverage" = `Race.coverageSec` from merged `WatchedInterval`s (gap tolerance 20s). "New coverage" = the frozen per-session `newCoverageSeconds`. "Rewatch" = timelinePlayed − newCoverage, apportioned to real time by the scope's average speed.

Personal records that already exist: longest session, most active day/month/year, longest consecutive editions (two different definitions). Most active day and year are computed but not rendered. Several others are cheap folds over data that is already loaded: most time in 7 days, races or Story Completes per month and year, unique coverage per day, start-to-complete gap.

Where the data is weak:
- `watchedAt` is a single timestamp, normally the time the stint was logged, because the log form has no date field. There is no start time, end time or pause data.
- `XPTransaction.createdAt` is the database insert time, not the stint's time.
- `newCoverageSeconds` is never rebuilt after a session is deleted.
- `realSeconds` can be inflated up to 10× by logging slow playback (0.1x), with no cap in RANGE mode.
- The unused `User.timezone` means buckets move if the machine's time zone changes.

Charting is recharts 3.10.1, used only in `statistics-view.tsx` (a monthly BarChart and an XP AreaChart).

risks: Real-time inflation: stored RaceViewingSession.realSeconds = timeline/speed with a speed floor of 0.1 and no cap in RANGE mode (session-engine.ts:61-86, playback.ts:13). One 24h race logged at 0.1x is a 240-hour 'session'. XP is guarded (xpMinSpeed 0.75, progression.ts:200), but stats, metrics.realHours, the existing realHours milestones (they pay XP) and any new Personal Records or hour milestones use the raw value. maxSessionRealHours=24 is only enforced on DURATION input (schemas.ts:150).

Timestamps are log times: there is no watchedAt input in the log form, so watchedAt, startedAt and storyCompletedAt are all 'when logged'. A user who logs a weekend's stints in one batch gets near-zero elapsed times, so 'fastest real-world completion' can be gamed and 'most time in a day' lands on the logging day. Intra-session crossing timestamps can only be interpolated. Floor any elapsed-time record at Σ realSeconds.

Year attribution of XP: XPTransaction.createdAt is the DB insert time (awardXp never sets it; verified in endurance.db). Backdated or seeded sessions, and any historical milestone backfill, will put XP and levels in the upgrade year unless createdAt is written explicitly. That in turn moves getLevelHistory and monthlyXpSeries.

newCoverageSeconds drifts: deleteViewingSession (session-engine.ts:465-536) and recomputeAllRaces never rebuild it on the remaining sessions. Per-day or per-year 'new coverage', rewatchShare and 'most unique coverage in a day' can be wrong after deletes. A backfill should replay each race's sessions in watchedAt order using addInterval with gapTolerance 20s.

Three definitions of 'completed': metrics (storyCompletedAt OR status==='COMPLETED', settable manually via setRaceStatusAction with no viewing, which is an existing milestone and achievement inflation path), stats-engine (Race.completedAt, never cleared on un-complete, race-engine.ts:88-90) and storyCompletedAt. New race-count milestones and records must key on storyCompletedAt.

Time zone instability: User.timezone is unused, and all day, month and year buckets use the server-process TZ at read time. Changing the machine TZ re-buckets history; a 23:30 Dec 31 stint can move year, so a 'completed' Wrapped can change. raceDate (UTC midnight) is read with local getFullYear in metrics.ts:209 and mastery-engine.ts:359, which shifts Jan-1 editions a year back west of UTC. dayPeriod().key is UTC (periods.ts:54) while stats use local keys.

Counter divergence: CareerProfile.lifetimeActiveDays/Weeks/longestStreakDays are incremental. They skip backdated days, use Monday weeks regardless of User.weekStart (momentum-engine.ts:363), and are never decremented on delete (a design rule). MomentumHistory is keyed by log `now`, not watchedAt. Do not use these as canonical sources for Year in Review or records; derive from sessions.

Performance: computeCareerMetrics loads every session on every stint inside the write transaction (session-engine.ts:261) and again on the dashboard and career pages. getStatistics issues ~50+ queries: per-year aggregates in loadActiveYears, up to 60 per-month XP aggregates, 4 per BudgetYear and 13 for challenges. They serialize on the synchronous better-sqlite3 adapter despite Promise.all. The isoWeekParts-per-row bucketing costs ~300 ms per 60k sessions unless memoized. There is no rollup table and no index on storyCompletedAt, startedAt or completedAt.

Design-rule landmines for new code: the literal 336 is banned in engines, domain, components and app (including string literals); new engine files must import @/lib/config; no Math.random in engines (Wrapped shuffles must be seeded); no decrements of permanent counters; banned scolding phrases; percentages must be scoped (never 'of all racing').
The stats-engine header comment says 'Postgres' (stats-engine.ts:47), but the DB is SQLite with DateTime stored as ISO TEXT (+00:00). Anyone moving bucketing into SQL would get UTC days.

Under a year filter, uniqueCoverageSeconds is the lifetime coverage of the races touched that year (by design). Reusing it as 'story seen this year' in Wrapped would overstate the year; use newCoverageSeconds (subject to the drift above).
questions_for_owner: Should Personal Records and hour-based milestones use raw real time (playback down to 0.1x, uncapped in RANGE mode)? Or 'credited' real time = timelineSeconds / max(speed, xpMinSpeed 0.75), capped at maxSessionRealHours, which matches how XP already works?

Stints store only a log timestamp. Is it acceptable to reconstruct in-session crossing moments and 'fastest completion' by assuming each stint ended at watchedAt and ran continuously? Or should the log form gain an optional start time (and should batch-logged stints be floored at Σ realSeconds)?

For Year in Review XP and levels: attribute by when the ledger row was written (XPTransaction.createdAt) or by the stint's watchedAt (possible for VIEWING/REWATCH via sessionId)? For backfilled milestone XP, should createdAt be the reconstructed achievement time (this rewrites the historical XP curve and level history) or the upgrade time?

Should a completed year's chapter or Wrapped be frozen (e.g. store a local-day key per session, or snapshot the year) so a later time zone change or session deletion cannot alter it? Or should it always be recomputed from canonical history? Should the unused User.timezone become authoritative?

'Most time in 7 days' and 'in a month': rolling windows, or calendar viewing weeks (User.weekStart) and calendar months? And does 'races completed in a month' mean Story Complete only, or also manual COMPLETED status / completedAt?
'336 hours in a calendar year': the fixed BUDGET_CONFIG.annualHours, or that year's (user-editable) BudgetYear.annualBudgetHours? Should rewatch time count toward it, as real time does today?

The existing MilestoneProgress ladders (realHours incl. 100..10,000, storyCompletes 10/25/50/100, racesCompleted 100..1000, stories12h/24h) and the Hall of Fame firsts already cover most of the requested Career Milestones and already pay XP. Should v0.4.0 migrate or rename them, or add a second parallel ladder (risking double rewards for the same event)?

When a session or race is deleted, should a Personal Record derived from it disappear or recompute (canonical history)? Or should records be landmarks that are never taken back, like achievements and Hall of Fame entries?

area: Mastery, achievements, milestones, collections, awards/Hall of Fame, trophies
summary:
Progression here is a set of idempotent "sync" engines. They run inside the single `logViewingSession` transaction, in this order (session-engine.ts:227-329): ensureMasteryTrees → ensureSeasonCollections → recomputeRaceMasteries → syncCollections → syncMastery → evaluateChallenges → computeCareerMetrics → syncAchievements → syncMilestones → season pass → syncAwards. Every engine that pays XP goes through `awardXp`, using a per-account unique `dedupeKey`. The locked/unlocked state is stored once and never cleared. Progress values are recomputed live from `CareerMetrics` (metrics.ts), and every engine measures itself against that same object.

"Milestones" already exist as their own system, separate from achievements. They are 14 numeric ladders in config/milestones.ts, each metric × threshold stored as a `MilestoneProgress` row with `reachedAt`, `valueAtReach` and `xpAwarded`, paid through dedupe `milestone:<metric>:<threshold>` and shown on the /achievements "Milestones" tab. The ladders already cover most of the requested Career Milestones: story completes 10/25/50/100, real hours 100…10,000, races completed 100…1,000, and the first 12h and first 24h. Achievements and Hall of Fame "first:*" and "milestone:*" plaques cover the same moments again.

None of the stored timestamps are historical. unlockedAt, reachedAt, storyCompletedAt and the HoF counting-ladder occurredAt are all the log/recompute `now`. XP rows are dated by the database at insert time.

`RaceMastery` together with `Race.iconicKey` is already the app's recurring-event model:
- It is per user and unique on `[userId, key]`.
- `Race.raceMasteryId` is the foreign key that links a race to its event.
- The aggregates are rebuilt from races on every stint.
- A RACE_EVENT mastery tree, keyed `event:<iconicKey>`, holds XP-paying nodes for editions 1/3/5/10, consecutive 3/5 and hours 50/150.

That model has several gaps:
- The key is free text: it is trimmed and capped at 80 characters, with no normalisation.
- The field only appears in the form when "Major event" is on, and turning that off clears it when the race is saved.
- Nothing is user-managed.
- The aggregate figures on `RaceMastery` are never displayed.
- Renaming a key creates a fresh tree that pays out again.

Hall of Fame and trophies record only firsts, story/hour/level plaques, major-event Story Completes, seasons, mastery trees, prestige, rare achievements and the season pass. There are no personal records. Awards grant no XP. Deleting a stint or a race never takes back achievements, milestones, mastery, trophies or HoF entries, or their XP; a test asserts this (the landmark test in tests/integration/session-flow.test.ts).
key_facts: MilestoneProgress (prisma/schema.prisma:563-579): userId, metric String, threshold Float, reachedAt DateTime?, valueAtReach Float?, xpAwarded Int, updatedAt; @@unique([userId, metric, threshold]). There is no sessionId, raceId or scope column. Rows are written only when a rung is reached (achievement-engine.ts:515-518); unreached rungs are not stored.

MILESTONES ladders (src/lib/config/milestones.ts:31-45): realHours and timelineHours use HOUR_STEPS [1,5,10,25,50,100,200,336,500,750,1000,1500,2000,3000,5000,7500,10000,15000,25000,50000]. racesCompleted and storyCompletes use COUNT_STEPS [1,5,10,25,50,100,200,350,500,750,1000,2000,5000]. Other ladders: championshipsCompleted, seasonsCompleted, circuits, countries, majorEventStories, stories24h [1,2,3,5,...], stories12h [1,2,3,5,...], sessions, careerXpMillions, level [5..1000]. All are lifetime metrics; none is per calendar year and none is per event.

syncMilestones (achievement-engine.ts:523-586): for every threshold at or below the current value that has no row, it pays awardXp source 'MILESTONE' with dedupeKey `milestone:${metric}:${threshold}` and amount milestoneXpFor (base 0.4 + 0.6×index, capped at 12×; MILESTONE_CONFIG economy.ts:565-600). It then upserts reachedAt=now and valueAtReach=the whole metric value after the stint, not the threshold. Several rungs crossed in one run all get the same `now`.

Milestone reads: getMilestoneBoard (achievement-engine.ts:736-829) takes reached state from the database and live values from metrics. Rendered at src/app/achievements/page.tsx:18-30 and src/components/dashboard/achievement-board.tsx:179+ ('Reached <date>'). The stint summary rebuild (src/lib/server/session-summary.ts:47,71-74) attributes milestones, achievements, mastery, trophies and HoF entries to a session using `reachedAt >= watchedAt - 5min`, a time-window heuristic with no session foreign key.

Two further meanings of 'milestone' exist: HoF plaques with category MILESTONE/CAREER and keys `milestone:stories:{10,50,100,500}`, `milestone:real-hours:{100,500,1000}` and `milestone:level:{10..1000}` (awards-engine.ts:731-764, AWARDS_CONFIG economy.ts:829-854); and season-pass tiers where `isMilestone` means every 10th tier (SeasonPassProgress.isMilestone).

Achievements (config/achievements.ts, 45 definitions): the Achievement definition table is upserted by syncAchievementDefinitions, which is called ONLY from src/app/achievements/page.tsx:16 and scripts/seed.ts:171,516. syncAchievements skips keys that have not been seeded (achievement-engine.ts:412-428), so unlocks are delayed on an account that has never opened /achievements.

Achievement unlock time: unlockedAt=now at the first sync where the condition holds (achievement-engine.ts:441,459). It is kept forever: `unlockedAt: row.unlockedAt ?? (conditionMet ? now : null)`. XP uses dedupe `achievement:${key}`. Unlocks are not revoked when a stint or race is deleted (session-engine.ts:460-463; landmark test at tests/integration/session-flow.test.ts:501-525), and their XP is not revoked either: revokeSessionXp only touches SESSION_BOUND_SOURCES ['VIEWING','REWATCH'] (xp-ledger.ts:164).

Achievements that overlap the requested Career Milestones: first_session (sessions≥1), lights_out (racesCompleted≥1), first_story (storyCompletes≥1), the_long_game (stories8h, runtime ≥7.5h), half_a_day (stories12h≥1), twice_around_the_clock (stories24h≥1), expedition (stories24h≥3; the name clashes with the new 'Race Expeditions' system), first_ten_hours/century_hours/five_hundred_hours/ironman/the_archive (realHours 10/100/500/1000/2500), first_dozen/half_century/centurion/five_hundred_stories (storyCompletes 12/50/100/500), annual_pilgrimage (longestConsecutiveEditions≥3), decade_of_devotion (maxEditionsOfOneEvent≥10). None covers a 6h race, racesStarted, a calendar-year total, or 5 or 25 editions.

CareerMetrics (metrics.ts:115-262) is recomputed in full on every stint. It loads every race plus every RaceViewingSession (findMany ordered by watchedAt, for longBreakReturns). Long-race thresholds are hard-coded 7.5/9.5/11.5/23 hours (metrics.ts:201-204) rather than read from MASTERY_SHAPE. Edition counting uses only `race.raceDate?.getFullYear()`, with no season fallback, and maxEditionsOfOneEvent = years.length, which counts duplicates (metrics.ts:208-213,233-236).

RaceMastery (schema.prisma:451-477): key (matches Race.iconicKey), name, editionsTracked, editionsStoryComplete, totalRealSec, totalTimelineSec (played, including rewatches), firstCompletedYear, latestCompletedYear, longestConsecutiveEditions; @@unique([userId, key]). Race.raceMasteryId is a foreign key with onDelete SetNull (schema.prisma:379-380), and there is an index on [userId, iconicKey].
recomputeRaceMasteries (mastery-engine.ts:769-849) rebuilds each event from its races on every stint (session-engine.ts:229) and in scripts/recompute.ts:78:
- editionsTracked counts all races with the key, including unwatched ones.
- editionsStoryComplete counts races, not distinct years.
- Years come from editionYear: raceDate.getFullYear() in server-local time, else the season year (mastery-engine.ts:358-362).
- It nulls raceMasteryId on races that no longer have an iconicKey (781-784).
- It never deletes or empties orphaned RaceMastery rows.
- The only other reader of RaceMastery is stats-engine.ts:2195, which reads key and name for the 'favourite event' label. No UI shows RaceMastery figures.

iconicKey input and naming: validation is optionalText(80), which trims and does nothing else (src/lib/validation/schemas.ts:110). Suggestions come from a datalist of MAJOR_EVENT_SUGGESTIONS (config/championships.ts:34-44: le-mans-24, daytona-24, sebring-12, nurburgring-24, spa-24, petit-le-mans, bathurst-12, indianapolis-8, suzuka-10) plus keys already in use (getIconicKeysInUse, src/lib/server/races.ts:294-304). The field is rendered only when the 'Major event' toggle is on (add-race-form.tsx:197-213, edit-race-form.tsx:176-183). updateRaceAction writes `iconicKey: input.iconicKey ?? null` (actions.ts:172), so saving with the toggle off erases the event link. Marking a race as a major event also multiplies its Story Complete bonus by majorEventStoryMultiplier 1.25 (economy.ts:59, progression.ts:237). The display name comes from the suggestion list or a title-cased key (mastery-engine.ts:510-519) and cannot be edited.

Mastery trees (schema.prisma:689-757): the tree key is 'global', `championship:${championshipId}` or `event:${iconicKey}` (mastery-engine.ts:66-74). ensureMasteryTrees creates and reconciles trees but never removes one (572-728). syncMastery creates a progress row for every node and never re-locks one (954). XP uses dedupe `mastery:${treeKey}:${nodeKey}` (984).

The event scope's metrics come from computeEventMetrics (mastery-engine.ts:307-309); inside an event scope, realHours counts all real time on its editions, including unfinished ones and rewatches.

Collections (collection-engine.ts): only kind SEASON is ever produced. CollectionKind MAJOR_EVENT, CIRCUIT and CUSTOM exist in the schema and in domain/types.ts:15 but nothing uses them. A card's filledAt = race.storyCompletedAt ?? completedAt ?? now (549). The Season Complete bonus uses dedupe `season-complete:${seasonId}` (584). Collection.completedAt is set to now (587); ChampionshipSeason.completedAt keeps its earlier value (592).

The awards engine (awards-engine.ts) is the only writer of Trophy and HallOfFameEntry. It pays no XP (header idea 5), and both tables are unique on [userId, key]. HoF firsts: first:race-completed, first:story-complete, first:race-12h, first:race-24h, first:major-event, first:season-complete, first:season-sweep, first:mastery-tree, first:season-pass (622-711). Per-race memory exists only for major events: trophy and HoF entry `major-event:${raceId}`, with details for race timeline, actual viewing time and session count (799-835). There is no general per-race Story Complete memory and no personal-best record anywhere in the museum.

HoF and trophy timestamps: occurredAt = race.storyCompletedAt for race-bound firsts and major events, collection.completedAt for seasons, and `now` for the count/hour/level plaques and for firsts during a backfill. The snapshot is the career frozen when the entry was recorded, taken from snapshotFromMetrics (345-360), not at the historical moment. getHallOfFame groups entries by occurredAt.getFullYear() (1225-1235), which already gives a per-year view.

Race.storyCompletedAt = `race.storyCompletedAt ?? now` at the recompute that first crosses the threshold (race-engine.ts:87), which is the log time, not session.watchedAt. updateRaceAction (actions.ts:180-181) and recomputeAllRaces use the default now, so a runtime edit can set storyCompletedAt to the edit time or clear it back to null. The log form never sends watchedAt (log-session-form.tsx:169-187), so in practice watchedAt is the log time, roughly the end of the stint. The seed passes now=watchedAt (scripts/seed.ts:289-301).

awardXp (xp-ledger.ts:58-127) cannot backdate: XPTransaction.createdAt uses the database default now(). rebuildCareerTotals re-stamps careerXpAfter/levelAfter ordered by [createdAt, id] (265-300). XPSource is stored as TEXT with no CHECK constraint (init migration, xp_transactions.source), so new enum values need no SQL migration. MAJOR_EVENT, HALL_OF_FAME, PRESTIGE and MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT currently have no writer.

Recompute and delete paths:
- scripts/recompute.ts:74-89 runs ensureMasteryTrees, ensureSeasonCollections, recomputeRaceMasteries, syncCollections, syncMastery, syncAchievements and syncMilestones. It does NOT call syncAwards.
- deleteViewingSession (session-engine.ts:465-545) revokes only session-bound XP and the story-complete bonus, then rebuilds totals.

overlaps.recommendation:
EXTEND this system rather than adding a third one. Rename the existing Milestones tab to Career Milestones.
- Add the missing definitions as new ladders or metrics in config/milestones.ts: racesStarted:1, a stories6h metric with a tolerance in MASTERY_SHAPE style, calendar-year real hours measured against BudgetYear.annualBudgetHours or BUDGET_CONFIG.annualHours (never a literal 336), and maxEditionsOfOneEvent 5/10/25.
- Keep the `milestone:` dedupe namespace so rungs already paid are never paid again.
- Add nullable columns to MilestoneProgress with ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, which is non-destructive: `achievedAt` (the exact reconstructed instant), `sessionId`, `raceId`, and a scope column for per-year and per-event rungs. The per-year and per-event rungs require widening the unique index; that is a DROP/CREATE INDEX, not a table rebuild.
- Keep `reachedAt` as the 'recognised at' time, so session-summary attribution and the rule against rewriting history both still hold.
- Backfill `achievedAt` by replaying sessions ordered by (watchedAt, createdAt, id), using a one-time instrumentation upgrade with a ConfigOverride marker in the same pattern as season-reset.

- Add nullable or defaulted columns: displayName override, userManaged/createdAt, circuitSlug/raceType hints, aliases (JSON), archivedAt, plus the new cached stats (edition count, hours, coverage, rewatch, longest edition, current streak).
- Make `key` immutable. Renaming changes only the display name; merging reassigns races and records an alias.

overlaps.existing: The achievement key `expedition` (Story Complete three 24h races, LEGENDARY, 30k XP). overlaps.recommendation: Store the Expedition Summary in its own table keyed by raceId, because HoF is curated and its rows are immutable. At most, mint one HoF plaque for 24h expeditions. Use a new dedupe namespace (`expedition:<raceId>:<pct>`) and a new XPSource value; neither needs an SQL migration. Rename or re-describe the `expedition` achievement in the UI copy so it does not collide with the system's name.

risks: An XP exploit already exists through mastery tree identity. Event trees are keyed `event:<iconicKey>` and championship trees `championship:<championshipId>`, and ensureMasteryTrees never removes the old tree. Renaming a race's iconicKey, or even changing its case (keys are not normalised), creates a fresh tree, and syncMastery pays every node again under new dedupe keys: up to 85,000 XP per event for the current raceEventNodes. Moving races to a newly created championship does the same with championship nodes. Event Legacy's user-managed rename and merge must not re-key trees.

Deleting and recreating a race is a second exploit. The story-complete dedupe key is per race id, and deleteRaceAction revokes nothing: orphaned viewing XP and the old story bonus survive until repairXpLedger, which only the dev script scripts/recompute.ts runs. Any new per-race award keyed by race.id (expedition checkpoints, legacy editions, HoF major-event) inherits this. Consider keying event awards by (eventId, editionYear) and revoking on race delete.

Deleting a stint never revokes achievement, milestone or mastery XP, and a test enforces it (session-flow.test.ts:501-525). One fabricated stint can therefore unlock one-shot rewards whose XP survives the deletion; the dedupe keys stop it being farmed repeatedly. The owner's 'no exploits via delete' constraint for the new systems conflicts with the design-rules test that forbids re-locking anything (`unlockedAt/awardedAt/completedAt: null`) outside upgrades/season-reset.ts.
Timestamps are unreliable for exact history:
- storyCompletedAt, unlockedAt and reachedAt are all the log or recompute `now`.
- Achievements unlock late when the Achievement rows were never seeded (the /achievements page was never visited).
- A runtime edit can clear storyCompletedAt and re-set it later.
- A backfill must replay RaceViewingSession history, not trust these columns. When sessions were backdated, replay order by watchedAt differs from the original log order.

Writing historical `achievedAt` values into reachedAt would break session-summary.ts. It attributes unlocks to a stint by `reachedAt >= watchedAt - 5min`, and a crossing earlier inside a long stint falls outside that window. Add a sessionId column instead of rewriting reachedAt.

Edition-year logic disagrees between engines. mastery-engine editionYear falls back to the season year; metrics.ts uses only raceDate and counts duplicate years in maxEditionsOfOneEvent. The decade_of_devotion achievement and the edition_10 node can therefore disagree. getFullYear() is server-local time while User.timezone exists. Two races with the same key in the same year (split broadcasts, duplicates) count twice in editionsStoryComplete but once in consecutive runs.

The UI couples iconicKey to isMajorEvent. To tag a non-major recurring event, a user must mark it major, which inflates the Story Complete bonus 1.25× and feeds majorEventStories achievements and trophies. Turning the toggle off in the edit form silently nulls iconicKey (actions.ts:172 with formValue returning undefined).

Race edits, status changes and deletions trigger no progression resync, so RaceMastery, trees, collections and awards are stale until the next stint. Event Legacy stats edited through a management UI must recompute synchronously.

scripts/recompute.ts does not run syncAwards, so a backfill that relies on it will not mint HoF or trophy entries. syncAwards also dates backfilled firsts and plaques at `now`, and snapshots carry today's career.

Name collisions: the dedupe prefix `milestone:` is taken by the ladders, the HoF keys `milestone:*` sit in another table, and the achievement key `expedition` exists. New systems need distinct prefixes and must not reuse `milestone:<metric>:<threshold>` unless they deliberately share rungs that are already paid.

The economy-balance test (tests/domain/economy-balance.test.ts) requires viewing XP to beat each other source and to be more than 40% of the total. New ladders added to MILESTONES are counted automatically; raceEventNodes are not modelled, so extra event nodes or expedition checkpoints could skew the economy without the test noticing.

Performance: computeCareerMetrics loads every session on every stint (metrics.ts:134-138), and syncAwards loads every trophy and HoF key. A full session replay for exact milestone timestamps must not run per stint; compute crossings incrementally from before and after totals and replay fully only in the upgrade backfill.

Literal-number rule: 336 must not appear in engines, domain, components or app (design-rules.test.ts:73-77). The calendar-year milestone must read BUDGET_CONFIG.annualHours or BudgetYear.annualBudgetHours. Note that actions.ts:509 already hard-codes 336, which slips through only because src/lib/server is not scanned.
questions_for_owner: Career Milestones: should they become the existing Milestones system (config/milestones.ts and MilestoneProgress, which already covers 10/25/50/100 Story Completes, 100–10,000 hours, 100–1,000 races and the first 12h and 24h), with added firsts, exact timestamps and per-year and per-event rungs? Or should they be a separate catalogue that sits beside it?

Many requested Career Milestones have already paid XP as ladder rungs, achievements and mastery nodes (for example, 100h currently pays century_hours 3,000, milestone realHours:100, global_hours_100 4,000, and a HoF plaque). Should the curated Career Milestones be XP-free presentation, with XP only for genuinely new rungs such as the first 6h, 336h in a calendar year, and 5 or 25 editions?

Event Legacy milestones (1/3/5/10/25 editions, 3/5/10 consecutive, 25/50/100/250 hours): should they be implemented as extra XP-paying RACE_EVENT mastery nodes, which is the one existing mechanic? Or as XP-free legacy badges, leaving mastery as the only paying layer? And should the existing event_hours_50/150 nodes stay as they are?

When a stint or race is deleted and a milestone is no longer true, should its achievedAt and XP remain (the current 'landmarks are never revoked' rule, enforced by tests)? Or does 'no exploits via delete' mean the new systems should revoke XP the way Story Complete bonuses are revoked?
Recurring-event identity: may users rename, merge and split events? If two events are merged, both existing mastery trees keep their unlocks, and no node pays twice. Is that the behaviour you want?
Should a race be able to belong to a recurring event without being marked a Major Event? That flag currently gates the field and also adds a 1.25× Story Complete bonus.
What defines an edition's year: raceDate, the season year, or a new explicit editionYear? And how should two races with the same event and the same year count (split broadcasts, re-uploads)?

Backfilled milestone XP can only be dated at upgrade time (awardXp cannot backdate; ledger createdAt is DB now()), so that XP would appear in the 2026 Year in Review rather than the year the milestone was actually reached. Is that acceptable, or should the ledger gain an occurredAt?

'Configurable' thresholds: is editing config files enough, which is how everything works today (the ConfigOverride runtime merge described in config/index.ts does not exist)? Or do you want per-user settings UI, which would make thresholds per-account and complicate dedupe keys and economy balance?

summary:
The whole UI runs off a small set of pieces. src/app/layout.tsx resolves the session once. It renders SideNav (a desktop rail from lg up) and TopNav (a sticky, horizontally scrolling bar below lg). Both come from a single flat `NAV` array in src/components/layout/nav.tsx:110-125: 14 items, no groups. A link counts as active by prefix match (nav.tsx:127-130), so nested routes such as /races/[id]/expedition, /stats/records or /career/milestones highlight their parent without any change to the nav. Pages are async server components. The pattern is: `requireUserId()`, then `ensureCareer()`, then fetch, then a `PageHeader` and a `mx-auto max-w-{3xl..6xl}` column of `Panel`s. Client views receive plain data. There are no loading.tsx, error.tsx or Suspense boundaries anywhere, so every page renders fully on the server before anything is sent.

The visual language is 'instrument cluster'. Everything is built from Panel, PanelHeader, PanelBody, Stat, TimingBar, ProgressRing, Badge, RarityBadge, EmptyState and SectorRule (src/components/ui/primitives.tsx). Controls are Button, Segmented, Toggle, Select and Field (controls.tsx), plus a native-<dialog> Dialog (dialog.tsx). The app is dark only. Themes change nothing but `--accent` and `--accent-soft`, set through `data-theme` on <html> (globals.css:94-102; the theme list is also duplicated in config/rewards.ts:101-106). Charts are Recharts 3.10, used in exactly one place: statistics-view.tsx. src/components/charts/ exists but is empty.

Celebrations have three levels: QUIET, NOTABLE and SPECTACULAR. `chooseCelebration` (session-engine.ts:415-435) picks the level, and StintSummary renders it inline on the race page with the `rise` keyframe. SPECTACULAR means a raised panel, an accent border, an accent-soft gradient and bigger figures. There is no confetti, no full-screen overlay and no slideshow component yet. Reduced motion is handled by one global CSS rule (globals.css:208-214) and nothing in JavaScript.

The race page already has the long-race pieces Expeditions needs: TwentyFourHourClock, drawn when runtime >= `TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR_CONFIG.longHaulThresholdSec` (12h); RaceTimeline, which draws the merged canonical intervals with gaps hatched; and GapList ('Still to watch'). Statistics is a client-side tabbed view (Overview, Cadence, Breakdown, Career) whose filters live in the URL. It already has a year-by-year table, month-by-month bars, XP by month, levels reached with dates, and the longest session.

Rules are enforced by source-scanning tests: tests/domain/design-rules.test.ts and the tone tests. They cover requireUserId and force-dynamic on pages, no DB access or XP awarding from components, engines importing config, banned literals (336, 1.35), a regex that forbids re-locking fields, and forbidden phrases. There are also two CSS gotchas: `text-base` is a colour, not a font size, and cn()/twMerge silently drops the custom font-size tokens.

area: Balance/config architecture, challenges and season pass interplay, test infrastructure, docs, release plumbing
summary:
All balance constants live in src/lib/config. Most of them are in economy.ts, which holds 22 `*_CONFIG`/`*_SHAPE` blocks plus LEVEL_TITLES and CHALLENGE_NOMINALS. The rest are in sibling modules (achievements.ts, milestones.ts, rewards.ts, championships.ts), and index.ts re-exports all of them. index.ts also builds DEFAULT_CONFIG, and a test requires every `*_CONFIG`/`*_SHAPE` block in economy.ts to be reachable from it. The convention: `*_CONFIG` says how much something is worth, `*_SHAPE` holds curves, thresholds and presentation settings. Every block is `as const` and every number has a comment explaining why. The comments promise a runtime override layer (`runtime.ts`/`loadConfig`), but it does not exist. The ConfigOverride table is only a per-account key/value store, used for preferences and upgrade markers.

The economy is anchored on watching. A real hour of new coverage pays 1,800 XP, a re-watched hour 450. A Story Complete pays 500–7,500, about 14–17% of that race's viewing XP. Achievements pay 200 (COMMON) up to 250k (MYTHIC). Milestone rungs pay from 300 up to about 13.7k at the top of their ladders (a few ladders reach 20–25k). Mastery event trees pay 85k per event. Challenges pay a base of 300, 1.5k, 5k or 15k by scope, scaled by 0.5–2.2x.

economy-balance.test.ts models a career at 7 stages. At every stage, watching must out-earn each other source on its own and be more than 40% of all XP. The binding stage is 20h, where watching is at 44.1%: only about 8.3k more XP from other sources fits there.

Challenges and the season pass recompute their progress from sessions. They award XP through awardXp with dedupe keys. Season XP is paid only by viewing, Story Complete, challenges and completing a season. All of those pay 0 until local midnight 1 Oct 2026, the reopening date set in SEASON_CLOSURE_CONFIG.

Tests run under Vitest against a real SQLite test database that migrates itself. Integration tests share one file serially (fileParallelism false). design-rules.test.ts enforces architecture and tone against the source. The Electron e2e script is run by hand. CI runs generate, desktop build, typecheck, lint and test. A v* tag builds the Windows installer.

The version is written in package.json, package-lock.json (twice) and changelog.ts. CHANGELOG.md is generated from changelog.ts. Everything else reads package.json.

questions_for_owner: Should the new Career Milestones and Event Legacy milestones pay any XP? Nearly every listed threshold (first race/Story Complete, 10/25/50/100 Story Completes, 100–10,000 hours, 100–1,000 races, 3/5/10 editions, 3/5 consecutive) already pays through milestone ladders, achievements and mastery. Should they be celebration-only, or pay only for the rungs that nothing else covers?

For the historical backfill on upgrade: should any XP rows be stamped with the reconstructed first-achieved time (this rewrites past XP graphs, levels and year chapters) or with the upgrade time (a one-off lump in 2026)? Or should the backfill record timestamps only and grant no XP?

Expedition checkpoint XP: should it follow the data like the Story Complete bonus (taken back if deleting a stint drops coverage below a checkpoint, then earnable once more) or stay earned permanently like achievements? If a race is switched to expedition mode after it has passed 50%, should the 10/25/50 checkpoints pay retroactively?

What should the default expedition threshold be: the existing 12h longHaulThresholdSec (which already drives the 24-hour clock, strategist stints and the spectacular celebration) or something lower, such as 6h? Should changing it be a per-account setting, and if so, is it retroactive?

How large a checkpoint pool is 'small'? One option consistent with the numbers: about 50% of the race's Story Complete band, split across the 5 checkpoints. That is 3,750 XP for a 24h race (~8.7% of its 43,200 viewing XP) and 1,500 for a 12h race. The alternative is flat daily-challenge-sized amounts (150–600 each).
Should the 336-hours-in-a-year milestone follow BUDGET_CONFIG.annualHours (so it moves if the budget is rebalanced) or be fixed at 336?
Should Event Legacy replace the RACE_EVENT mastery trees, or sit alongside them as the profile and history page, with XP staying in the mastery nodes?

Should economy-balance.test.ts be widened in 0.4.0 to model every XP source, including the challenge XP and event mastery that it currently omits, so the 'watching is the main source' rule is actually enforced for the new systems?
